says: The fur, as promised, and I mean to do it your way without flinching: about six thousand short strokes, each one laid along the direction the coat actually grows, hard for the tabby stripes and light between them, in three sittings with a sharpening after each. No outline at all. If the cat has an edge it will be because the hairs stop. Her eyes and the bib of white on her chest stay nearly bare. As for the letter: I do fight my letters, but Ines gets the fair copy. The envelope is blank because I have not decided to send it.

ops.text: She woke up for this and does not think it is a likeness.
